docs.title: Act I: The Looking Glass of Time — Waves, Energy & The Cosmic Horizon
docs.text:
🎬 Synchronized Simulation: Watch Act I in Cinema Studio ▶ Play Act I

When you gaze into the night sky, you are never witnessing the cosmos as it currently exists. Because light propagates at a finite speed, every celestial observation is fundamentally an archaeology of the past.

This introduces a foundational question in modern observational astrophysics: How far back in cosmic history can humanity peer based on hard observational evidence, and where does observational evidence terminate—forcing us to rely on theoretical physics confirmed by particle colliders?

To establish this boundary, we must examine the physical vehicle carrying every cosmic message: The Physics of Waves.

Every wave—whether sound, water, or light—is governed by three fundamental properties:

  1. Speed (\(c\)): The speed of a wave is determined by the medium it travels through. Across the vacuum of space, light travels at the universe's absolute speed limit: \(c pprox 299,792 ext{ km/s}\).
  2. Wavelength (\(\lambda\)) & Frequency (\(f\)): Wavelength is the spatial distance between two successive wave peaks, while frequency is the number of wave cycles passing a fixed point per second:
\[ c = \lambda \cdot f \]
  1. Energy (\(E\)): As quantum mechanics proved, a photon's energy is directly locked to its frequency:
\[ E = h \cdot f = rac{h \cdot c}{\lambda} \]

High-frequency waves pack intense, lethal energy—like Gamma rays, X-rays, and Ultraviolet light. Low-frequency waves carry gentle, low energy—like Infrared, Microwaves, and Radio waves.

docs.title: The Cosmic Twist: Cosmological Redshift
docs.text:
As starlight traverses billions of light-years, it does not journey through static, Newtonian space. The fabric of spacetime itself is continually expanding. And as spacetime stretches, it physically stretches the traveling wave of light!

Its wavelength elongates, its frequency steadily drops, and the wave loses energy:

\[ 1 + z = rac{\lambda_{ ext{observed}}}{\lambda_{ ext{emitted}}} = rac{a(t_{ ext{observed}})}{a(t_{ ext{emitted}})} \]

Where \(z\) is the Cosmological Redshift and \(a(t)\) is the cosmic scale factor of the universe.

This explains a foundational mystery of astronomy: When the universe first became transparent, 380,000 years after the Big Bang, it unleashed a blinding, white-hot flash of optical light at 3,000 Kelvin. Yet over 13.8 billion years of expanding space, that ancient light was stretched by a factor of 1,100 times (\(z pprox 1100\)). Its frequency collapsed, cooling down to a frigid, uniform blackbody temperature:

\[ T(z) = T_0 \cdot (1 + z) \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad 3,000 ext{ K} \;\longrightarrow\; 2.725 ext{ K} \]

That is why the oldest evidence of creation—the Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation (CMBR)—is detected today not as blazing visible light, but as cold, faint microwaves at 2.725 Kelvin!

docs.title: Act II: The Theoretical Horizon — Singularity, Inflation & The Primordial Atom
docs.text:
🎬 Synchronized Simulation: Watch Act II in Cinema Studio ▶ Play Act II

Rewind the cosmic clock 13.8 billion years. There were no stars, no galaxies, no matter, and no empty space. There was neither a "before" nor an "outside." All of existence was locked inside a single geometric point of infinite density, infinite temperature, and zero volume: The Point of Singularity.

docs.title: The Planck Epoch: Quantum Gravity Frontier (10⁻⁴³ s)
docs.text:
Here, General Relativity collides with Quantum Mechanics, and all known equations of physics cease to operate. The fundamental Planck timescale represents the boundary of known quantum gravity:

\[ t_{ ext{Planck}} = \sqrt{ rac{\hbar G}{c^5}} pprox 5.39 imes 10^{-44} ext{ seconds} \]

During the Planck Epoch, temperatures stood at an unimaginable:

\[ T pprox 10^{32} ext{ Kelvin} \]

The four fundamental forces of nature—Gravity, the Strong Nuclear Force, the Weak Nuclear Force, and Electromagnetism—were fused into a single, unified Superforce.

docs.title: Cosmic Inflation: Exponential Metric Expansion (10⁻³⁶ s)
docs.text:
As the primordial cosmos cooled, spontaneous symmetry breaking ruptured the Superforce. First, Gravity tore away. Then, at \(10^{-36}\) seconds, the Strong Nuclear Force decoupled, triggering the cataclysmic epoch of Cosmic Inflation.

As theoretical physicist Alan Guth demonstrated, in less than a trillionth of a trillionth of a second, spacetime expanded exponentially driven by the scalar inflaton field:

\[ a(t) = a_i \cdot e^{H t} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad ext{Expansion Factor} > 10^{78} \]

This hyper-luminal expansion flattened the spatial curvature of spacetime, permanently solving the Horizon and Flatness Problems and explaining why the cosmic sky is so astonishingly uniform in every direction.

docs.title: The Higgs Field & Hadron Formation (10⁻¹¹ to 10⁻⁵ s)
docs.text:
In the wake of Inflation, the universe was an ultra-dense, turbulent Quark-Gluon Plasma. Yet fundamental particles could not roam freely: they collided with the omnipresent Higgs Field. Through the Higgs mechanism, quarks and leptons acquired mass, dragging their velocities below the speed of light.

As the temperature dropped past \(10^{12} ext{ Kelvin}\), gluons bound the quarks into the first stable hadrons:

\[ u + u + d \;\longrightarrow\; p^+ \quad (938.3 ext{ MeV}), \qquad u + d + d \;\longrightarrow\; n^0 \quad (939.6 ext{ MeV}) \]

docs.text:
Between the third and twentieth minutes, the universe acted as a single, cosmic thermonuclear reactor. Protons and neutrons fused into Deuterium, and then into Helium-4 nuclei:

\[ p + n \;\longrightarrow\; ext{D} + \gamma \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad \,^4 ext{He} \quad (75\%\ ext{H},\; 25\%\ ext{He}) \]

The primordial elemental composition of the universe was carved in stone: 75% Hydrogen, 25% Helium-4, and trace Lithium-7.

Yet, reality remained pitch-black for 380,000 years because free electrons continuously scattered all photons through Thomson scattering:

🎬 Synchronized Simulation: Watch Act III in Cinema Studio ▶ Play Act III

As spacetime relentlessly expanded over 380,000 years, the cosmic temperature steadily decayed. And when the universe reached precisely 380,000 years of age, a foundational law of physical chemistry formulated in 1920 by legendary Indian astrophysicist Meghnad Saha took command:

\[ rac{n_{i+1} n_e}{n_i} = rac{2 g_{i+1}}{g_i} \left( rac{2\pi m_e k_B T}{h^2} ight)^{3/2} \exp\left(- rac{\chi_i}{k_B T} ight) \]

Where \(\chi_i = 13.6 ext{ eV}\) is the ionization potential of Hydrogen. The cosmic temperature fell to exactly 3,000 Kelvin (\(2,700\ ^\circ ext{C}\)). Thermal kinetic energy plummeted below the 13.6 electron-volt threshold. In an instant, protons captured free electrons into stable quantum shells, creating the universe's first neutral atoms: Neutral Hydrogen.

This historic watershed is known as The Epoch of Recombination. And the moment free electrons were locked away, the fog cleared. Optical depth dropped to zero:

\[ au = \int n_e \sigma_{ ext{T}} c \, dt \;\longrightarrow\; 0 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad ext{Cosmic Transparency} \]

Trapped photons were liberated to travel freely across the cosmos in straight lines: Photon Decoupling. In a single cosmological heartbeat, the universe became crystal-clear and transparent!

docs.title: The Cosmic Evidence Ladder
docs.text:

The mottled red and blue patches on Planck's map represent temperature variations of only one part in 100,000—a mere \(18\ \mu ext{K}\)! These are the primordial Baryon Acoustic Oscillations—sound waves vibrating through the embryonic plasma that gathered dark matter and hydrogen gas, igniting the Cosmic Dawn!

docs.title: Act IV: The Deepest Gaze — Expanding Spacetime, Hubble & The JWST Revolution
docs.text:
🎬 Synchronized Simulation: Watch Act IV in Cinema Studio ▶ Play Act IV

In 1929, American astronomer Edwin Hubble analyzed the spectral absorption lines of distant nebulae, making an astounding discovery: Every distant galaxy exhibited a systematic shift toward longer, redder wavelengths. He formulated Hubble's Law:

\[ v = H_0 \cdot d, \qquad H_0 pprox 70 ext{ km/s/Mpc} \]

The velocity of recession is directly proportional to distance: the farther a galaxy lies, the faster it recedes from Earth! Expanding spacetime stretches the traveling waves of light passing through it.

In 1998, astronomers measuring Type Ia Supernovae—exploding white dwarf standard candles—uncovered a second revolutionary shock: Approximately 5 billion years ago, cosmic expansion began speeding up (Accelerating Expansion), driven by Dark Energy (\(\Lambda\)), which constitutes over \(68.3\%\) of the total cosmic energy density:

\[ \Omega_\Lambda pprox 68.3\%, \qquad \Omega_m pprox 26.8\%, \qquad \Omega_b pprox 4.9\% \]

docs.text:

  • James Webb Space Telescope (JWST): Stationed \(1.5 ext{ million km}\) away at Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2), equipped with gold-coated beryllium mirrors and NIRCam. In May 2024, JWST shattered all astronomical records by confirming galaxy JADES-GS-z14-0:
\[ z = 14.32 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad t_{ ext{lookback}} = 13.51 ext{ Billion Years} \quad (\mathbf{290 ext{ Myr after Big Bang}}) \]

This discovery proved that massive stars formed far earlier than anticipated, initiating the reionization epoch.

docs.title: The Stellar Lifecycle: The Cosmic Family Tree & The Periodic Table
docs.text:
Now that the first stars were blazing across the cosmos... how did they live, evolve, and die? To understand how the elements of the Periodic Table were created, we must trace the cosmic family tree of all stars: The Stellar Lifecycle.

Every star begins inside a vast, cold Nebula—a nursery of interstellar gas and dust. Under gravity, dense pockets collapse into dark, compact Bok Globules, governed by the Jeans Instability Criterion:

\[ M > M_J pprox \left( rac{5 k_B T}{G \mu m_H} ight)^{3/2} \left( rac{3}{4\pi ho} ight)^{1/2} \]

Condensing further into a glowing, rotating Protostar.

Here, mass dictates cosmic destiny!

  • If an embryo gathers less than eight percent of the Sun's mass (\(M < 0.08\ M_\odot\)), its core never reaches the 10 million Kelvin needed for hydrogen fusion. It becomes a Brown Dwarf—a failed star drifting in the dark.
  • But if it crosses that critical \(0.08\ M_\odot\) mass threshold, thermonuclear fusion ignites! The star enters the Main Sequence, spending millions or billions of years in stable hydrostatic equilibrium.

docs.title: The Divergence of Stellar Destiny
docs.text:
When hydrogen in the core is finally exhausted, stellar destiny splits into two radically divergent paths:

  1. For Low-to-Intermediate Mass Stars (like our Sun, \(M < 8\ M_\odot\)): The star expands into a swollen Red Giant. Its core begins fusing helium, and eventually it gently puffs off its outer layers into a glowing, iridescent Planetary Nebula. At its center remains a dense, Earth-sized degenerate stellar ember: a White Dwarf, which over trillions of years will cool into a silent Black Dwarf.

  2. For Massive Stars (exceeding eight solar masses, \(M > 8\ M_\odot\)): They swell into colossal Red Supergiants! Inside these cosmic giants, gravity crushes the core to extreme temperatures, fusing fuels in concentric onion-like shells:

\[ ext{Hydrogen} \;\longrightarrow\; ext{Helium} \;\longrightarrow\; ext{Carbon \& Oxygen} \;\longrightarrow\; ext{Silicon \& Sulfur} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbf{Nickel ext{-}62\ \&\ Iron ext{-}56} \]

  • Adding a proton to Helium-4 forms Lithium-5, which decays in \(10^{-22} ext{ s}\).
  • Fusing two Helium-4 nuclei forms Beryllium-8, which decays in \(10^{-16} ext{ s}\).

docs.title: Fred Hoyle & The 7.65 MeV Carbon Resonance
docs.text:
In the early 1950s, English astrophysicist Fred Hoyle reasoned backward from the existence of life: If Carbon exists in human hands, stars must have found a way to forge Carbon-12 via the Triple-Alpha Process (\(3 imes {}^4 ext{He} o {}^{12} ext{C}\)).

Hoyle predicted that Carbon-12 must possess an undiscovered, excited quantum resonance level at precisely 7.65 MeV! William Fowler tested this at Caltech and confirmed the Hoyle State at exactly \(7.654 ext{ MeV}\), amplifying fusion by millions of times:

\[ 3 \,^4 ext{He} \;\longrightarrow\; \,^8 ext{Be} + \,^4 ext{He} \;\longrightarrow\; \,^{12} ext{C}^* (7.654 ext{ MeV}) \;\longrightarrow\; \,^{12} ext{C} + \gamma \]

In the landmark 1957 B²FH paper (Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler, Hoyle), the truth was cemented: Every heavy element in your body was synthesized inside stars. We are all stardust.

docs.title: The Chandrasekhar Limit & Supernova Nucleosynthesis (1.44 Solar Masses)
docs.text:
Iron represents the most tightly bound nucleus in the cosmos. Fusing beyond iron consumes energy rather than releasing it. When an iron core forms, radiation pressure vanishes, resisted only by Electron Degeneracy Pressure.

In 1930, 19-year-old Indian student Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar proved that electron degeneracy has an unyielding physical ceiling:

\[ M_{ ext{Chandrasekhar}} pprox rac{\omega_3^0}{4\pi}\left( rac{h c}{G} ight)^{3/2}\left( rac{Z}{A m_H} ight)^2 pprox 1.44\ M_\odot \]

The moment the collapsing iron core exceeds \(1.44\ M_\odot\), relativistic gravity crushes electrons into protons:

\[ p + e^- \;\longrightarrow\; n + u_e \]

In a fraction of a second, an iron core the size of Earth collapses into a ball of pure neutrons just twenty kilometers wide! The infalling outer star slams into this incompressible neutron ball and detonates: A Type II Core-Collapse Supernova!

In this blast, free neutron densities exceed \(n_n > 10^{20} ext{ neutrons/cm}^3\). Through the r-process (Rapid Neutron Capture), atomic nuclei gorge on neutrons faster than they decay, forging the heaviest elements in the universe:

\[ au_n \ll au_ eta \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad \,^{56} ext{Fe} + n \;\longrightarrow\; \dots \;\longrightarrow\; \,^{197} ext{Au},\; \,^{195} ext{Pt},\; \,^{238} ext{U} \]

What remains behind is an ultra-dense Neutron Star, or if the core exceeds three solar masses, it collapses into a Black Hole!

docs.title: The Grand Cosmic Loop & Star Generations
docs.text:
The supernova shockwave hurls all these forged heavy elements back into interstellar space, seeding a brand new, enriched nebula!

  • Population III Stars: The pristine first generation, born of pure Hydrogen and Helium with zero metals.
  • Population II Stars: Old, metal-poor stars formed from early enriched gas.
  • Population I Stars (Our Sun): Third-generation stars born billions of years later from rich, recycled nebular gas containing iron, silicon, carbon, and oxygen—making rocky planets and life possible!

docs.title: The Thermodynamic Paradox
docs.text:
The Second Law dictates that total entropy must increase (\(\Delta S > 0\)). How could cosmic gas assemble into ordered solar systems? Through Gibbs Free Energy:

\[ \Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0 \]

As atoms bind together, they release binding heat (\(\Delta H\)). Radiating this heat into the freezing 2.725 Kelvin vacuum heat sink of space causes an astronomical entropy surge in the universe:

\[ \Delta S_{ ext{universe}} = rac{Q}{T_{ ext{sink}}} \qquad (T_{ ext{sink}} = 2.725 ext{ K}) \]

Purchasing local planetary order at the cost of global cosmic entropy!

The Hidden 5-Stage Prompt Compiler
docs.text:
When a user submits a simple one-line prompt to platforms like Trickle.so, v0, or Lovable, the platform does not pass raw text to LLMs like Gemini 3.1 or Claude. It processes the prompt through an automated multi-stage compilation pipeline:

[User Short Command] 
   └──> Stage 1: Domain & Intent Classifier (e.g., Academic/Earth Sciences)
   └──> Stage 2: Meta-Prompt Expander (Generates structured creative brief)
   └──> Stage 3: Design Token & Primitive Injection (Tailwind + shadcn + Lucide)
   └──> Stage 4: High-Throughput LLM Generation (Gemini 3.1 / Claude 3.7)

docs.title: 11. Fluvial Geomorphology & River Bend Migration (Ikeda-Parker-Sawai Model)
A. Scientific Core & Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
Based on our deep study of Ryan Sael's River Bend Lab (https://sael.net/river-bend/), the simulation implements the classic Ikeda, Parker & Sawai (1981) meander migration theory in its discrete 1D formulation established by Howard & Knutson (1984):

  1. Hydraulic Geometry (Manning's Equation):
  2. Sinuosity index: \(\sigma = \frac{L_{channel}}{L_{valley}}\), modifying the effective reach slope \(S = \frac{S_{valley}}{\sigma}\).

  3. Channel depth \(H\) and mean cross-sectional flow velocity \(U\): $\(H = \left(\frac{Q \cdot n}{W \sqrt{S}}\right)^{0.6}, \quad U = \frac{Q}{W \cdot H}\)$ where \(Q\) is discharge (\(20 - 400\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)), \(W\) is channel width (\(90\text{ m}\)), and \(n = 0.03\) is Manning's roughness.

  4. Near-Bank Velocity Perturbation (\(A[i]\)):

  5. Water around a bend is accelerated along the outer cut bank and retarded along the inner point bar. The velocity anomaly is governed by both local curvature \(\kappa(s)\) and an upstream-lagged convolution representing fluid inertia and secondary circulation development: $\(\alpha = \frac{2 C_f}{H} \quad (C_f = 0.02, \text{ Darcy-Weisbach / Chezy friction})\)$ $\(num_i = \kappa_i + e^{-\alpha \Delta s} num_{i-1}, \quad den_i = 1 + e^{-\alpha \Delta s} den_{i-1}, \quad \overline{\kappa}_i = \frac{num_i}{den_i}\)$ $\(A[i] = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{W}{2} (\omega \kappa_i + \Gamma \overline{\kappa}_i), -A_{max}, A_{max}\right)\)$ with \(\omega = -1\) (local bank boundary curvature term), \(\Gamma = 2.5\) (upstream curvature memory coefficient), and \(A_{max} = 0.6\).

  6. Near-bank velocities: $\(u_{outer} = U(1 + A[i]), \quad u_{inner} = U(1 - A[i])\)$

  7. Excess Shear Stress Bank Erosion (\(e\)):

  8. The outer bank (cut bank cliff) scours only when near-bank boundary velocity exceeds the critical erodibility threshold \(u_c = 1.35\text{ m/s}\) (corresponding to critical entrainment shear stress \(\tau_c\)): $\(e = M \cdot \max\left(0, \left(\frac{u}{u_c}\right)^2 - 1\right) \quad (M = 5\text{ m/yr})\)$

  9. Point Bar Sediment Accretion (\(d\)):

  10. On the inner bank, secondary helical flow decelerates water below the settling threshold \(u_d = 1.25\text{ m/s}\). Suspended and bedload sediment drops to build point bars: $\(d = K_d \cdot C_{eff} \cdot \max\left(0, 1 - \left(\frac{u}{u_d}\right)^2\right) \quad (K_d = 5)\)$ where effective sediment load \(C_{eff} = C_{in} + \beta \cdot \overline{e}\) reflects upstream bank collapse feedback.

  11. Centerline Migration Vector & Width Relaxation:

  12. Centerline lateral displacement rate: $\(mig_i = \frac{(e_R - d_R) - (e_L - d_L)}{2}\)$ Nodes are displaced along the local normal vector: \(\vec{x}_i \leftarrow \vec{x}_i + \vec{n}_i \cdot (mig_i \Delta t + \text{noise})\).

  13. Width \(W\) relaxes toward equilibrium hydraulic geometry (\(W_{eq} \propto Q^{0.4}\)) over decadal timescales \(T_w \approx 60\text{ yr}\).

  14. Neck Cutoff & Oxbow Lake Formation:

  15. As sinuosity increases, meander loop necks narrow. When the Euclidean distance between two non-adjacent channel points falls below critical neck width: $\(\Delta r_{neck} < 1.6 \cdot W\)$ an instantaneous neck cutoff occurs. The meander loop is abandoned, isolating an oxbow lake (billabong) that progressively fills with fine clay plugs, while the active river straightens, abruptly reducing sinuosity.

  16. Helical / Secondary Flow (The Corkscrew):

  17. Centrifugal acceleration propels high-velocity surface water toward the outer cut bank, creating vertical downward scouring and undercutting.

docs.title: B. Performance & Resource Weight Audit: 3D Heavy vs. Zero-Build Lightweight
docs.text: Addressing the critical question regarding computational load: - Why sael.net is Resource-Heavy: - The heavy load is not caused by the river math, but by the lavish desktop-grade 3D showroom rendering: 1. 2.5 Million Pixel Budget (rendering at high devicePixelRatio). 2. 6-Stage Postprocessing Pipeline: 4x MSAA Scene Pass, 2048x2048 PCF soft shadows, Ground Truth Ambient Occlusion (GTAO) with 12 samples, Half-Float UnrealBloomPass, 72-tap Poisson gather Depth of Field (MacroDOF), and SMAA anti-aliasing. 3. Planar Floor Mirror Reflection: A secondary camera (reflCam) re-renders the complete scene geometry every frame with oblique clipping planes. 4. Dual 32-Bit Float GPU Render Targets: Dynamically writing distance fields and historical age stamps into GPU memory. - Result: 14–20 ms per frame on high-end GPUs, causing battery drain and thermal throttling on mobile devices. - Why the Mathematical Simulation is Featherlight: - The Howard-Knutson 1D centerline ODE operates on just 40 to 80 nodes! - Manning depth calculation, curvature convolution, excess shear erosion, and neck cutoff detection require less than 0.15 ms per timestep on standard JavaScript. Stepping 30 simulated years per second consumes less than 2% of a single CPU thread. - Our Zero-Build Adaptation Strategy: - Instead of a GPU-punishing 3D flume tank, we deploy a lightweight HTML5 2D Canvas / WebGL2 topographic ribbon: - 60 FPS, < 1% CPU utilization, 0% idle load, perfectly responsive on mobile phones. - Interactive Controls: Discharge slider (\(Q: 20 - 400\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)), Sediment concentration slider (\(C: 0 - 2\text{ g/L}\)), Time scrubber (\(0 - 1200\text{ yr}\)), and live telemetry dials for Sinuosity (\(\sigma\)) and Cut Bank erosion velocity (\(m/\text{yr}\)). - Helical Flow Cross-Section Popover: Interactive vector cutaway displaying the corkscrew flow (cyan outward surface vector, amber inward bed return vector). - Oxbow Lake Timeline: Chronological color coding of abandoned loops and clay plug infill history.

docs.title: 12. Generative Blueprints, 3D Solvers & Video Scrubbing Architecture
A. The 7-Stage Incremental Builder ("Jelly Study" Protocol)
docs.text:
• Problem: Monolithic 3D prompt requests fail because LLMs mix physics, geometry generation, UI state, and raycasting all at once, creating unstable code.
  • Architectural Solution: The 7-stage constraint chain:
  • Visual Foundation: Stage, camera orbit, static geometry, typography behind 3D (pointer-events: none).
  • Soft-Body Physics: Localized point picking, volumetric deformation solver, elastic settlement, GPU acceleration fallback.
  • Multi-Asset Scaling: Dynamic object instantiation, collision bounds, contextual radial menus.
  • Planar Geometric Slicing: Dynamic clipping planes with closed manifold cap triangulation (preventing hollow mesh holes).
  • Topological Stacking: Rigid skewer constraint running through soft-body centers, maintaining outer elasticity without exploding.
  • Input Bifurcation: Touch event disambiguation (1-finger drag = deform, empty canvas = camera orbit, pinch = zoom, tap = menu).
  • Performance & Leak Prevention: Zero per-frame memory allocation, disposal of removed meshes/buffers, GPU budget cap.

docs.title: B. Anti-Jitter Video Scrubbing (CursorScrubVideo & Scroll Engine)
docs.text:
• Key Breakthrough: Continuous video playhead scrubbing driven by mouse coordinates or scroll position without browser playback lag.
  • Critical Technical Guards:
  • All-Keyframe Encoding: Must encode video with All-Intra (-g 1 -keyint_min 1 -x264-params "scenecut=0" via FFmpeg). Standard inter-frame compression creates 200–500ms seek latency.
  • Seek Storm Prevention: Only assign video.currentTime = next if !isSeeking and Math.abs(video.currentTime - next) > 0.008s.
  • Silent Buffer Trick: Call video.play().then(() => video.pause()) on mount to force GPU hardware frame decoders to initialize immediately.
  • Lerp Damping: RAF loop with next = current + (target - current) * smoothing (smoothing 0.15–0.25).

docs.title: 14. Code-Drawn Vector Animation & Visual Keyframe Pipelines (html-anime & html-animator)
A. html-anime Architecture (Prompt-to-Code Animation Without Video Models)
docs.text:
• Origin & Core Philosophy:
  • Reverse-engineered from blixvip/html-anime (https://github.com/blixvip/html-anime.git).
  • Completely eliminates heavy .mp4 video downloads, GPU-taxing generative video models, and AI hallucination artifacts.
  • Draws cinematic animation entirely in pure HTML5, vector SVG, and GSAP 3 timelines, adhering to the HyperFrames specification.
  • The HyperFrames Standard:
  • Strict composition metadata: data-composition-id, data-start, data-duration, data-track-index.
  • Exposes timeline instances to the global browser scope: window.__timelines[slug] = tl;, enabling external frame scrubbing and video capture tools.
  • The 5-Skill Agent Discipline:
  • html-anime-direct (The Shot Sheet Contract):
    • Fixed, deterministic runtimes: 8s (3 shots: Establish \(\to\) Sakuga \(\to\) Button), 12s (4 shots), or 20s (6 shots).
    • The 1-Sakuga Constraint: Exactly ONE expensive action shot per scene. All other shots are static holds, atmospheric pans, or subtle character pauses. This guarantees deterministic completion and eliminates code sprawl.
    • Closed Color Script: Every scene is constrained to strictly 10 hex codes (e.g., sky, ink, moon, accent, practical, iris, skin, hair, sclera, line). No arbitrary off-palette colors.
  • html-anime-cel (Flat Cel Painting):
    • Strict z-index depth order from background to foreground: $\(\text{Sky} \longrightarrow \text{Far Silhouette} \longrightarrow \text{Ground / Wide Figures} \longrightarrow \text{Atmosphere / Weather} \longrightarrow \text{Close Hero} \longrightarrow \text{Type}\)$
    • Hard-edged shadows (e.g., ink at 20% opacity over local color) — no fuzzy gradients or airbrush blur.
    • Deterministic particles and rain coordinates (never unseeded Math.random()).
  • html-anime-timing (Traditional Anime Cadence):
    • Animates on "twos" (12 drawings/s in a 24 FPS container) and holds.
    • Stepped opacity toggling (tl.set) between discrete SVG poses instead of continuous rubbery tweening, replicating authentic hand-drawn cel animation.
    • Directional speed lines, smear frames, and tapered blade/motion arcs.
  • html-anime-camera (Cinematic Lens & Cutting):
    • Symmetrical framing, wide-shot atmospheric silhouettes vs. close-up vector detail.
    • The Color-Dip Cut: An opaque full-screen accent color flash (#dip overlay, duration \(\approx 0.3\text{s}\)) to transition between shots without jump cuts.
  • html-anime-render:
    • Zero-dependency, pure web execution runnable directly in any browser without build tooling.

docs.title: B. Mathematical Time-Space Framework
docs.text:
1. The Global Discrete Card Indexer (Rt(s, m)):
  2. Given normalized continuous progress \(s \in [0, 1]\) and \(m\) cards/specimens: $\(s' = \text{clamp}(s, 0, 1) \cdot m\)$ $\(\text{index} = \lfloor s' \rfloor, \quad \text{local} = s' - \text{index}\)$
  3. index: Designates the currently active focal item in the sequence (\(0, 1, \dots, m-1\)).

  4. local: Fractional sub-step progress (\(0.0 \to 1.0\)) driving the active card transition and secondary background reactions.

  5. Closed-Form Physics & Built-in Easing Suite:

  6. Natural Bézier Solver: Custom Newton-Raphson solver evaluating cubic-bezier curves with bisection fallback: $\(\text{natural} = \text{cubic-bezier}(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)\)$
  7. Snappy Exponential Ease-Out: $\(f(t) = 1 - 2^{-10t}\)$
  8. Polynomial Overshoot (Zero Spring Library Overhead): $\(f(t) = 1 + 3.2(t - 1)^3 + 2.2(t - 1)^2\)$
  9. Damped Harmonic Elastic Bounce: $\(f(t) = 2^{-10t} \cdot \sin\left(\left(10t - 0.75\right) \cdot \frac{2\pi}{3}\right) + 1\)$
  10. Smooth Cubic Hermite: $\(f(t) = \begin{cases} 4t^3 & \text{if } t < 0.5 \\ 1 - \frac{(-2t + 2)^3}{2} & \text{if } t \ge 0.5 \end{cases}\)$

docs.title: The 7 Core Architectural Engines:

1. LOOKS Engine (60 Effects, 300+ Pre-Configured Looks):

  3. DEPTH Engine (Monocular Depth Map Estimation & 2.5D Spatial Parallax):
  4. Automatically computes depth displacement maps \(Z(x, y)\) from 2D luminance and neural depth estimations.
  5. Extrudes flat 2D layers into virtual 3D perspective cards with camera mouse-tracking tilt, plane rotations, and SVG extrusions without loading heavy 3D asset files.
  6. GLOW Engine (Three-Dial Optical Post-Processing):
  7. Bloom: Multi-pass Gaussian blur thresholding creating radiant light scattering around high-luminance elements.
  8. Streaks: Anamorphic horizontal optical flare distortion mimicking high-end cinema lenses and laser spectrometers.
  9. Trails: Frame-accumulation temporal persistence creating fluid motion smear and phosphor decay.
  10. MOTION Engine (Procedural Micro-Animations & Timeline Loops):
  11. Trigonometric procedural physics loops (Float, Breathe, Drift, Sway, Pop-in) that animate rotation, scale, and position without external animation library overhead.
  12. Kinetic typography engine with character-by-character cascade delays and undulating sine waves.
  13. SOUND Engine (Audio-Reactive Frequency Spectrum Modulation):
  14. Uses Web Audio API AnalyserNode with Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) splitting incoming audio into 4 distinct frequency bands:
    • Sub-Bass / Kick (\(20 - 120\text{ Hz}\)): Drives shockwaves, scale pulses, and violent displacement surges.
    • Bass (\(120 - 350\text{ Hz}\)): Modulates chromatic aberration and thermal palette offsets.

  15. TRACK Engine (Feature Tracking & Optical Flow Layer Anchoring):
  16. Edge and contrast centroid tracking that pins synthetic visual elements, data telemetry tags, or callouts to moving focal points in image/video feeds.

docs.title: D. Mathematical & Physical Formulation of Atmospheric Dynamics
docs.text:
By abstracting Ladybug's visual filters into physical solvers, we transform image-stylization shaders into rigorous synoptic meteorological simulators:

  1. Atmospheric State Variables & The Ideal Gas Law:

  2. The scalar barometric pressure field \(P(x, y)\) and temperature field \(T(x, y)\) govern local air density \( ho(x, y)\) through the dry air equation of state: $\( ho(x, y) = rac{P(x, y)}{R_d \cdot T(x, y)}\)$ where \(R_d = 287.058 ext{ J}/( ext{kg}\cdot ext{K})\) is the specific gas constant for dry air.

  3. Pressure Gradient Force (PGF):

  4. The fundamental driving force accelerating air parcels from high pressure cells toward low pressure sinks: $\(\vec{F}_{ ext{pgf}} = - rac{1}{ ho} abla P = - rac{1}{ ho}\left( rac{\partial P}{\partial x}\hat{i} + rac{\partial P}{\partial y}\hat{j} ight)\)$

  5. Coriolis Acceleration & Geostrophic Balance:

  6. On a rotating sphere with angular velocity \(\Omega = 7.2921 imes 10^{-5} ext{ rad/s}\) at latitude \(\phi\), the Coriolis parameter is \(f = 2\Omega\sin\phi\).
  7. In geostrophic equilibrium (above the planetary boundary layer where surface friction is negligible), the horizontal PGF is exactly balanced by the Coriolis force: $\(\vec{F}_{ ext{pgf}} + \vec{F}_c = 0 \implies -2\Omega\sin\phi \cdot (\hat{k} imes \vec{v}_g) = rac{1}{ ho} abla P\)$
  8. Decomposed into Cartesian velocity components: $\(u_g = - rac{1}{f ho} rac{\partial P}{\partial y}, \quad v_g = rac{1}{f ho} rac{\partial P}{\partial x}\)$

  9. Visual Implication: Winds blow parallel to isobars rather than across them! Cyclonic circulation flows counter-clockwise around Lows in the Northern Hemisphere, while anticyclonic circulation flows clockwise around Highs.

  10. Thermal Wind Relation (Baroclinic Shear):

  11. The vertical shear of the geostrophic wind is directly proportional to horizontal temperature gradients: $\( rac{\partial \vec{v}_g}{\partial \ln p} = - rac{R_d}{f}\left(\hat{k} imes abla_p T ight)\)$

  12. Explains the formation of the Subtropical Westerly Jet Stream (STWJ) over the Indo-Gangetic Plains and Himalayas due to the steep meridional temperature gradient between the equator and Tibetan landmass.

  13. Orographic Lift & Adiabatic Thermodynamic Profiles:

  14. When moist air encounters topographic barriers (e.g. the Dhauladhar & Pir Panjal ranges of Himachal Pradesh), forced vertical displacement \(w = \vec{v}\cdot abla Z_s\) triggers adiabatic expansion:
    • Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (DALR): \(\Gamma_d = rac{g}{c_p} \approx 9.8^\circ ext{C/km}\) (unsaturated ascent up to Lifting Condensation Level, LCL).
    • Saturated Adiabatic Lapse Rate (SALR): \(\Gamma_s \approx 5.0 - 6.5^\circ ext{C/km}\) (condensation releases latent heat of vaporization \(L_v \approx 2.5 imes 10^6 ext{ J/kg}\)).

docs.title: Recipe 1: Fast 2.5D Monocular Depth Displacement (DEPTH Engine)
docs.text:
Extracts luminance from any image/diagram to displace vertices on cursor hover: 

function applyDepthParallax(canvas, image, mouseX, mouseY) {
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  const W = canvas.width, H = canvas.height;
  const offX = (mouseX / W - 0.5) * 24; // Parallax tilt angle
  const offY = (mouseY / H - 0.5) * 18;

  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
  // Layer 1: Background shadow with depth offset
  ctx.save();
  ctx.translate(-offX * 0.5, -offY * 0.5);
  ctx.filter = 'blur(12px) brightness(0.2)';
  ctx.drawImage(image, 0, 0, W, H);
  ctx.restore();

  // Layer 2: Foreground specimen with 2.5D perspective displacement
  ctx.save();
  ctx.translate(offX, offY);
  ctx.drawImage(image, 0, 0, W, H);
  ctx.restore();
}

docs.title: Recipe 2: Audio-Reactive FFT Parameter Dial (SOUND Engine)
docs.text:
Captures microphone or audio tracks and binds frequency energy to UI dials: 

class AudioDialController {
  constructor() {
    this.audioCtx = new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)();
    this.analyser = this.audioCtx.createAnalyser();
    this.analyser.fftSize = 512;
    this.buffer = new Uint8Array(this.analyser.frequencyBinCount);
  }
  getBands() {
    this.analyser.getByteFrequencyData(this.buffer);
    // Sub-Bass (0-120Hz): bins 0 to 3
    const kick = (this.buffer[0] + this.buffer[1] + this.buffer[2]) / (3 * 255);
    // Mid-Range (350-2500Hz): bins 8 to 58
    let midSum = 0;
    for (let i = 8; i <= 58; i++) midSum += this.buffer[i];
    const vocals = midSum / (51 * 255);
    return { kick, vocals }; // Returns normalized 0.0 to 1.0 values
  }
}

docs.title: Recipe 3: Ordered \(4\times 4\) Bayer Matrix Dithering (Pixel Dither G0)
docs.text:
Converts scalar density into tactile stipple textures: 

const BAYER_4X4 = [
  [ 0,  8,  2, 10],
  [12,  4, 14,  6],
  [ 3, 11,  1,  9],
  [15,  7, 13,  5]
];
function renderBayerDither(ctx, x, y, value0to1, color) {
  const threshold = BAYER_4X4[y % 4][x % 4] / 16.0;
  if (value0to1 > threshold) {
    ctx.fillStyle = color;
    ctx.fillRect(x, y, 1, 1);
  }
}

docs.title: Recipe 4: Multi-Stop Chromatic Thermal LUT (Thermal Pink)
docs.text:
Maps continuous temperature \([-15^\circ\text{C}, 42^\circ\text{C}]\) to FLIR heat colors: 

function getThermalColor(T) {
  const norm = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (T + 15) / 57));
  if (norm < 0.25) { // Deep Cryo Indigo -> Electric Cyan
    const f = norm / 0.25;
    return `rgb(${Math.round(7 + f * 5)}, ${Math.round(10 + f * 190)}, ${Math.round(36 + f * 190)})`;
  } else if (norm < 0.50) { // Electric Cyan -> Spring Mint
    const f = (norm - 0.25) / 0.25;
    return `rgb(${Math.round(12 + f * 81)}, ${Math.round(200 + f * 40)}, ${Math.round(226 - f * 58)})`;
  } else if (norm < 0.75) { // Spring Mint -> Amber Gold
    const f = (norm - 0.50) / 0.25;
    return `rgb(${Math.round(93 + f * 162)}, ${Math.round(240 - f * 56)}, ${Math.round(168 - f * 91)})`;
  } else { // Amber Gold -> Thermal Pink -> White Hot Core
    const f = (norm - 0.75) / 0.25;
    return `rgb(${Math.round(255 - f * 19)}, ${Math.round(184 - f * 112)}, ${Math.round(77 + f * 76)})`;
  }
}

docs.title: Recipe 5: Continuous Trigonometric Isoline / Isobar Generator
docs.text:
Draws razor-sharp contour lines without marching squares mesh generation: 

function renderIsobarLine(ctx, gx, gy, step, pressureVal, interval = 4) {
  // Evaluates sine modulo at standard intervals (e.g. 4 hPa)
  const isoSine = Math.sin((pressureVal - 980) * Math.PI / interval);
  if (Math.abs(isoSine) < 0.18) {
    ctx.fillStyle = pressureVal < 1004 ? 'rgba(236, 72, 153, 0.9)' : 'rgba(2, 210, 227, 0.9)';
    ctx.fillRect(gx, gy, step, step);
  }
}
